subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chat support automatic durable per-sender agent provisioning, and what identity, authorization, quota/lifecycle, and shared/private memory boundaries should become the public contract?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear, but implementing it would create durable agents, workspaces, configs, skills, memory namespaces, and message-routing authority from group-chat senders, which is a product and security boundary decision rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Design generic contract first
options.body: Create a generic admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and memory isolation contract, then let Feishu implement it as a channel-owned capability.

options.title: Keep session-only routing
options.body: Keep current groupSessionScope and explicit thread-bound subagent mechanisms, documenting that full per-user group orchestration is not core behavior yet.

options.title: Reject automatic provisioning
options.body: Close this feature direction if maintainers decide group identities must never create durable OpenClaw agents automatically.

recommendation.title: Design generic contract first
recommendation.body: Create a generic admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and memory isolation contract, then let Feishu implement it as a channel-owned capability.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses Feishu plugin behavior, core routing contracts, security defaults, and VISION.md product guardrails, and steipete has the strongest recent history across those surfaces.
